title: Head - Human Resources
description:
**Position summary**

**Job title** Head – Human Resources

**Company** Dhanraj Global Corporation Pvt. Ltd. (DGC)

**Department** Human Resources

**Location** Head office, Navi Mumbai, with regular visits to project sites

**Reports to** Managing Director

**Works closely with** Directors, Chief Legal Officer, Finance, Project and Sales heads

**Team** None at present. This is a standalone role to begin with; DGC is open to building an HR team under this role as the function grows

**Employment type** Full-time, permanent

**Experience** 7–12 years in HR including experience running HR end to end for a company or business unit

**Compensation** Commensurate with experience and industry standards

**Salary Range** ₹12,00,000 – ₹24,00,000 CTC per annum

**Role purpose**

The Head – Human Resources sets up and personally runs every people process for DGC's real estate business, from hiring and payroll to policy, compliance and performance management, in line with DGC's documented HR SOPs.

DGC is a real estate development group with residential, plotted and commercial projects across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. This role covers the real estate business only; the group's hospitality operations are outside its scope. It is moving from promoter-driven to professionally managed operations. This role builds the HR backbone that transition needs: documented policies, audit-ready records and consistent processes across head office and project sites.

**What to expect in this role**

This is a hands-on, individual role to begin with, and candidates should apply with that understanding.

· **You are the HR department.** You will start without a team. You will do the work yourself: screening CVs, issuing offer letters, processing payroll inputs, maintaining files and drafting policies.

· **Strategy and execution sit with the same person.** You will design the appraisal system and also run it. You will write the leave policy and also answer the leave queries.

· **Support comes from other departments, not from reports.** Finance, Legal, site administration and external vendors (recruitment partners, payroll and compliance consultants) will work with you, but none of them report to you.

· **The team comes later, and you will build it.** DGC is open to adding HR team members as headcount and workload grow. You will make the case for those hires and recruit them yourself.

The role suits someone who has run HR single-handedly or in a very small team, and who prefers building a function to inheriting one.

**Key responsibilities**

You will carry out each of the following yourself, with operational support from Finance, Legal, site administration and external vendors where noted. All HR work is to be carried out as per DGC's documented HR SOPs, using the prescribed forms and registers.

**1. HR strategy and organisation design**

· Build the HR roadmap in line with DGC's growth and project pipeline.

· Define the organisation structure, reporting lines, role descriptions and approval matrices (DoA) for all verticals with the Managing Director.

· Plan manpower for new projects and sites with department heads.

**2. Talent acquisition**

· Handle hiring end to end: requisitions, sourcing, screening, interview scheduling, offers and background verification.

· Manage recruitment partners, job portals and campus channels within approved budgets.

· Hire for leadership, professional and site roles on agreed timelines.

**3. Onboarding and employee lifecycle**

· Run onboarding, induction, probation reviews, confirmations, transfers, promotions and exits.

· Maintain complete, audit-ready personnel files and the HRMS database.

· Conduct exit interviews and report attrition trends with root causes.

**4. Performance management**

· Design and run the annual goal-setting and appraisal cycle (KRAs / KPIs) across all levels.

· Link performance outcomes to increments, incentives and promotions.

· Guide department heads on performance improvement plans.

**5. Compensation, benefits and payroll**

· Maintain salary structures and grades benchmarked to the real estate market.

· Prepare and verify monthly payroll inputs, and work with Finance for accurate, on-time processing and statutory deductions.

· Administer benefits, insurance, leave and reimbursement policies.

**6. Learning and development**

· Assess training needs and run an annual training calendar covering technical, safety, soft-skill and leadership programmes.

· Track training effectiveness and maintain training records.

· Build succession plans for key roles.

**7. Policies, SOPs and governance**

· Follow DGC's documented HR SOPs, policies, forms and registers in every HR process, without informal deviations.

· Ensure employees and department heads follow the HR SOPs, and report non-compliance to the Managing Director.

· Propose improvements to the HR policy manual, code of conduct and SOPs through the formal amendment process; changes take effect only after approval.

· Prepare HR inputs for board and committee requirements.

· Keep HR documentation ready for due diligence by investors, lenders and auditors.

**8. Statutory and labour-law compliance**

· Ensure compliance with applicable labour laws and the Labour Codes, including PF, ESIC, gratuity, bonus, minimum wages and the Maharashtra Shops & Establishments Act.

· Check contractor and site labour compliance (contract labour licences, BOCW registrations, wage and attendance registers) with project teams.

· Constitute and run the Internal Committee under the POSH Act, including training and annual reporting.

· Coordinate labour inspections and statutory audits with the Chief Legal Officer.

**9. Employee relations and engagement**

· Handle grievances, disciplinary proceedings and domestic enquiries fairly and on record.

· Run engagement surveys, recognition programmes and internal communication.

· Build a performance-driven, professional culture across head office and project sites.

**10. HR operations and analytics**

· Implement and administer an HRMS for attendance, leave, payroll and records.

· Publish a monthly HR dashboard to the Managing Director: headcount, hiring, attrition, cost, training and compliance status.

· Prepare and manage the HR budget, including the case for future HR hires.

**Qualifications, experience and skills**

**Essential**

· MBA / PGDM in HR, or a Master's in Labour Welfare / Personnel Management (MLW, MPM or MSW-HR).

· 7–12 years of progressive HR experience across recruitment, HR operations, payroll, compliance and performance management.

· Experience running HR end to end, either as the sole HR person or as the senior-most HR person in a small team.

· Strong working knowledge of Indian labour laws, the Labour Codes, POSH and statutory payroll compliance.

· Hands-on experience with an HRMS and payroll for a multi-location workforce.

**Preferred**

· Experience in real estate, construction or infrastructure.

· Experience setting up an HR function, policies or an HRMS from scratch.

· Experience in a company with institutional investors or formal board governance.

· Experience with site and contract workforces.

**Skills and attributes**

· Comfortable doing operational work personally, without waiting for a team.

· Process-disciplined: follows documented SOPs, keeps records current and holds others to the same standard.

· Clear written communication: policies, SOPs and board-ready reports.

· Firm, fair and discreet in handling employee matters.

· Data-driven, comfortable with Excel, HR dashboards and audit trails.

· Fluent in English, Hindi and Marathi.

· Willing to travel to project sites.

**Why join DGC**

· Shape the HR function of a 39-year-old real estate developer with a growing pipeline of residential, plotted and commercial projects.

· Report directly to the Managing Director, with visible impact on how the company is run.

· Play a central role in DGC's move toward institutional governance and professional management.

· Grow with the function: the person who builds it will be the one to lead the team as it is hired.
